paper_metadata.title: Risk of seizure recurrence after a first unprovoked seizure in childhood

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides a clear description of the target population, recruitment setting, and inclusion/exclusion criteria. The sample size is large for a single-center study, and the recruitment process appears systematic.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: children aged 1 month to 16 years, who were attended to between November 1, 2008 and October 31, 2016 following a first seizure.
items.reasoning: The age range and clinical context (first seizure) are explicitly defined.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: our hospital covers the population of Naka-Harima and Nishi-Harima, west of Hyogo, Japan, and provides pediatric emergency care and specialized outpatient care in pediatric neurology
items.reasoning: The authors describe the hospital's role as a regional center for emergency and specialized care, suggesting a representative catchment area.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between November 1, 2008 and October 31, 2016
items.reasoning: Specific dates are provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Japanese Red Cross Society Himeji Hospital, Hyogo, Japan
items.reasoning: The specific institution and location are named.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Children who had been diagnosed with definite epileptic seizure were included, while children who had had non-epileptic events and provoked seizures were excluded... Children with absence seizures, myoclonic seizures, epileptic spasms, and previous unprovoked seizures were excluded.
items.reasoning: Detailed criteria for both inclusion and exclusion are provided, including specific seizure types.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: During the study period, 495 patients with a first unprovoked seizure visited... 467 patients to be included in the study.
items.reasoning: The participation rate is high (94.3%), with only 28 patients excluded (15 for referral/no EEG, 13 for starting treatment).

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1 shows the clinical characteristics of the patients. The mean age of the patients was 6.3 ± 4.4 years and the median age was 5.7 years.
items.reasoning: Table 1 provides a comprehensive list of sex, seizure type, etiology, EEG findings, and neuroimaging.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports a very high follow-up rate for a long-term study, with over 95% of patients followed for at least 2 years. The methods for follow-up (visits or telephone) are appropriate.

items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: 95.2% of patients were followed-up for greater than 2 years and 61.0% were followed-up for greater than 5 years.
items.reasoning: The retention rate is excellent for a 10-year longitudinal study.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (recurrence) is clearly defined, but its measurement relies partly on parental recall via telephone interviews, which introduces a risk of recall bias, although this is standard in epilepsy prognosis studies.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Recurrence was defined as an unprovoked seizure occurring more than 24 h after the first seizure.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined using standard ILAE criteria.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: followed-up at hospital visits or by telephone every 6 months to ascertain seizure recurrence.
items.reasoning: While 6-month intervals limit recall bias, telephone reporting is less reliable than clinical observation or EEG confirmation of every event.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: the children were followed-up at hospital visits or by telephone every 6 months
items.reasoning: The follow-up protocol was applied consistently to the cohort.
